newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares flat, profit-taking tempts investors.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares flat, profit-taking tempts investors.

text.p: Norwegian shares tracked sideways on Tuesday despite continuing positive sentiment and new record highs on other European bourses.
Brokers said investors might be tempted to begin a bout of profit-taking following Oslo's 11-session streak of record closes, which came to a halt on Monday.
The Total index sliped 0.1 percent to end at 924.24 points as turnover dropped almost 50 percent from Monday to 761.75 million crowns.
Market attention was focused on exploration and production group Saga Petroleum amid speculation that the company had clinched a takeover of UK-based Sante Fe from the Kuwaiti state.
Saga's A share slipped two crowns to 106 crowns, while the B relinquished 2.50 crowns to 97.50 crowns. Trade was relatively light in the stock.
"If you look at the deal in terms of value per barrel of proven reserves Sante Fe comes out at about $6 per barrel while Saga is $3 per barrel at today's reserve level," said a broker.
"Why buy Sante Fe when Saga's cheaper? I can understand that some investors are not too keen for Saga to make this deal."
